It takes real honesty to notice these patterns and ask this question, so I want to acknowledge that. What you're describing—drinking more than you intend, anger you don't usually feel, and lingering guilt even on nights when nothing "goes wrong"—are things worth paying attention to. That persistent guilt may be your mind signaling that alcohol is affecting you in ways that don't sit right with your values, even when there's no obvious incident to point to.

None of this means you're a bad person, and it doesn't have to define you. It could be helpful to talk with a doctor or a counselor who can look at what's underneath the drinking and help you figure out next steps without judgment. If you're open to it, tracking when and why you drink might also reveal patterns worth understanding. You're clearly reflecting carefully here, and reaching out for support would be a strong, caring thing to do for yourself.
